gaps.sentence: He behaves as if he were ___ owner of the company.
gaps.explanation: 'The owner' — there is one owner, so 'the'.

gaps.sentence: This is ___ second time you've been late this week.
She works as ___ waitress during the summer holidays.
gaps.explanation: After 'as' and 'work as', jobs take a/an: work as a waitress.

gaps.sentence: It was ___ honour to meet the ambassador.
gaps.explanation: 'Honour' starts with a vowel sound (silent h), so 'an honour'.
'The capital of Italy' — the of-phrase makes it unique and definite.

gaps.sentence: ___ information you sent was extremely helpful.
gaps.explanation: 'The information you sent' — the clause defines it; information is uncountable.

gaps.sentence: She put ___ money in the safe before leaving.
gaps.explanation: 'The money' and 'the safe' are specific in the situation.

gaps.sentence: He demands ___ answer before the end of the day.
